title: The 10 Best Rechargeable Work Lights
subtitle: Magnetic, handheld, tool-battery and tripod work lights for engine bays, crawl spaces and job sites, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A rechargeable work light puts bright light exactly where you're working (under a hood, in a cabinet, in a crawl space) with no cord to trip on. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (a magnetic base, USB-C charging, a water-resistance rating and a tool-battery platform). Pocket mechanic lights stick to the car; tool-battery lights from DEWALT run on packs you already own; flood and tripod lights light a whole area. They run from about $10 for a Coquimbo 2-pack to $60 for Klein's MODbox area light or a cordless tripod light.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

products.name: Coquimbo 2 Pack Rechargeable Work Light, Magnetic, 5 Modes
products.verdict: Two pocket-size magnetic lights for $10, the best seller here, with a hook, five modes and USB-C charging.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX LED Work Light, Rechargeable Flashlight, Pivoting Head, Bare Tool (DCL050)
products.best_for: DEWALT 20V owners who need area light on the job.
products.verdict: The highest-rated work light here: three LEDs at 1,000 or 300 lumens, a head that pivots 140°, and a telescoping hook that hangs from 2-inch pipe or studs, on any DEWALT 20V battery.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX LED Work Light/Flashlight (DCL040)
products.best_for: DEWALT owners who want a long-running flashlight.
products.verdict: DEWALT's classic 20V flashlight with a 120° rotating head and a hook. At 110 lumens it's a spotlight, not an area light, but it runs a long time on a 20V pack.

products.name: HOTLIGH Rechargeable Work Light, 5000mAh Magnetic Flashlight, 360° Rotate, 1200 Lumens
products.best_for: Mechanics: stick it to the car and aim it anywhere.
products.verdict: A machined-aluminum magnetic light with a 5,000 mAh USB-C battery, three light sources and a head that rotates 360° vertically and 180° sideways.

products.name: TRESDA 3000LM Rechargeable Work Light, Magnetic LED, Foldable & Portable
products.best_for: Lighting a whole engine bay or work area.
products.verdict: A folding three-panel light that shapes a wide beam around an engine bay, with four magnets, five modes, an IP65 rating and a believable 30 W / 3,000-lumen spec.

products.name: TRESDA 7000LM Rechargeable LED Work Light, 100W Portable Flood Light

products.verdict: A cordless flood light for a whole garage or campsite: 7,000 lumens from a stated 100 W, a 120° beam, a 10,800 mAh battery, a 360° stand and IP65 sealing.

avoid.name: DANCINGBOAR 120W Solar Rechargeable 144 LED Work Light, 10000LM Flood Light (RLW008)
avoid.flag: Claims 120 W and 10,000 lumens from a 14-oz pocket light
avoid.verdict: A $16 solar light sold on numbers it can't physically reach. For real area light, the TRESDA 7000 lists a 100 W system and a 10,800 mAh battery that fit its brightness.
reasons: It claims 120 W and 10,000 lumens from a 14-ounce, 6.5 x 4.3-inch light. The TRESDA flood light needs a 100 W system and a 10,800 mAh battery for 7,000 lumens.
Running 120 W from a battery small enough for that body would drain it in minutes, so the rating can't describe sustained output.
It lists no battery capacity or runtime for its brightest mode, the numbers you'd need to check the claim.

buyers_guide.q: How bright should a work light be?
buyers_guide.a: 300-1,000 lumens covers engine bays and cabinets. 2,000-7,000 lumens lights a garage or job area. Treat big numbers on small lights with suspicion; a stated wattage and battery size keep claims honest.
Magnetic pocket lights stick to car bodies and steel and charge by USB. Tool-battery lights (DEWALT, Klein) run longer and survive jobsite drops, and you probably already own the battery.
ANSI FL1 is a test standard for flashlight and work light output and runtime. An FL1 rating means the lumens and hours were measured the same way across brands.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need a water-resistance rating?
buyers_guide.a: For outdoor or wet work, yes. IP65 handles rain and splashes. Most pocket mechanic lights have no rating and shouldn't be left in the rain.
Runtime drops sharply on high. Pocket lights run 2-4 hours on high; tool-battery and large-battery lights run much longer. Check runtime at the brightness you'll actually use.
